title: Impinj M750 UHF Inlay (Monza R6-P) — AUTHENTICATE + Untraceable AES-128 RAIN RFID for Brand Protection, DPP, Pharma
summary: This Impinj long-range UHF inlay (Monza R6-P silicon class) is the brand-protection variant of the M700 family — adding 32 bits of user memory + full EPC Gen2v2 Untraceable, AUTHENTICATE, and Crypto Suite 3 (AES-128) on top of the M730's retail platform. Proud Tek supplies M750 inlays for cryptographic anti-counterfeit programmes, retail privacy at point-of-sale (Untraceable command), pharmaceutical serialisation with on-tag user data, EU Digital Product Passport UHF tier, and returnable transit item (RTI) cycle authentication. Pairs with Impinj's Authenticity cloud service for turnkey verification without operating an HSM. Brand owners, pharmaceutical compliance teams, and EU compliance integrators can use it as the chip / AUTHENTICATE / Untraceable / DPP / Authenticity-cloud reference.

brief.label: Chip silicon and lineage
items: Impinj M750 = rebranded Monza R6-P silicon under the M700-family naming refresh; datasheets, EPC Gen2v2 feature support, and TID prefix unchanged.
Existing readers, encoders, and inlays branded as Monza R6-P fully interoperable with M750 inlays.
Brand-protection tier of the M700 family above M730 — adds AUTHENTICATE + Untraceable + Crypto Suite 3 (AES-128) + 32-bit user memory.

brief.label: Memory architecture
items: 96-bit EPC (extensible to 128 via configuration) — SGTIN-96 / SSCC-96 / GRAI-96 / GIAI-96 encoding per GS1 TDS 2.0.
96-bit serialised factory-programmed TID for inventory deduplication and unique-tag identification.
32-bit user memory — sufficient for batch ID, expiration-date offset, encrypted serial fragment, DPP URL hash. Step up to UCODE 9 (32-224 bit configurable) when more user memory is needed.
32-bit access password + 32-bit kill password per EPC Gen2v2.

brief.label: Cryptographic features — AUTHENTICATE + Untraceable
items: AUTHENTICATE (AES-128 challenge-response per GS1 Crypto Suite 3) — chip-level proof that silicon is genuine Impinj R6-P, not relabelled lower-grade chip. Foundation for any UHF brand-protection programme.

Untraceable command — at point-of-sale or on-exit, chip can be commanded to return shortened EPC, hide TID, hide user memory until next power cycle. Standard pattern for GDPR-aware EU retail rollouts.
Crypto Suite 3 — AES-128 cryptographic primitive supported per ISO/IEC 18000-63:2015 Amendment 1.
Hide-EPC NOT supported on M750 (UCODE 9 supports it); programmes requiring Hide-EPC should specify UCODE 9.

brief.label: Sensitivity and read range
items: Read sensitivity: -22.0 dBm typical (datasheet) — ~0.6 dB below M730 (-22.6 dBm) due to additional cryptographic feature circuitry.
Write sensitivity: -18.0 dBm typical.
Free-air bench: 7-9 m on paper hangtag with Impinj R700 at +30 dBm EIRP. Real-world: 5-7 m apparel hangtag, 1.5-2 m on-metal with foam spacer, 1.0-1.5 m on-liquid.
For maximum read range with cryptographic AUTHENTICATE: NXP UCODE 9 (-23.0 dBm) is the alternative; for pure-EPC volume retail without AUTHENTICATE, M730 (-22.6 dBm) at lower silicon ASP.

brief.label: Air interface and standards
items: ISO/IEC 18000-63:2015 + Amendment 1 (AUTHENTICATE) air interface.
EPC Gen2v2 protocol 2.1 — full feature set including Untraceable, AUTHENTICATE, Crypto Suite 3.
GS1 EPC Tag Data Standard (TDS) 2.0 SGTIN encoding.
RAIN RFID Alliance certified; Walmart RFID mandate compatible (M750 also satisfies the SGTIN-96 source-tag requirement).

brief.label: Mid-market brand protection without an HSM
items: Cryptographic anti-counterfeit at UHF range without the silicon-ASP step up to NXP UCODE DNA.
M750 + Impinj Authenticity service combination removes the need for the brand owner to operate their own HSM / KMS — deployable in months rather than quarters.

Verification pattern: reader (fixed, handheld, or smartphone via NFC tunnel) issues AUTHENTICATE challenge; chip responds with CMAC-style proof; reader posts proof to Authenticity cloud REST API; API returns 'authentic' / 'not authentic' / 'unknown' in <200 ms typical.
Brand-owner integration cost: single REST API integration + UI flow on the verifier side. No on-premise key infrastructure. Typical proof-of-concept to production rollout: 4-6 weeks.

brief.label: Retail privacy at point-of-sale (Untraceable)
items: EU GDPR-aware retail rollouts use Untraceable command at POS to comply with consumer-tracking concerns.
POS reader sends Untraceable instruction at checkout; subsequent reads outside the store return 32-bit shortened EPC that cannot be tracked back to SKU.
Standard pattern for EU retail mandates where the same SGTIN-96 supply-chain tag must be neutralised for consumer-side privacy.
Chip restores full EPC on next power-cycle / unlock with access password — supports legitimate returns and warranty workflows.

brief.label: EU Digital Product Passport UHF tier
items: EU Regulation 2024/1781 (Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation) — Digital Product Passport mandates for textiles (2027), batteries, electronics expanding through late 2020s.
DPP guidance for UHF supports user memory holding the DPP URL pointer + chip-level AUTHENTICATE to prove carrier is genuine (anti-substitution).
M750's 32-bit user + AUTHENTICATE = minimum-feature DPP-compliant UHF chip.
For DPP profiles requiring larger on-tag data (full DPP URL + serial + sustainability fields), step up to NXP UCODE 9 with 224-bit configurable user memory.

brief.label: Pharmaceutical serialisation with on-tag fragments
items: DSCSA (U.S. Drug Supply Chain Security Act, FDA) and EU FMD (Falsified Medicines Directive) — serialised SGTIN encoding primarily lives in backend keyed by EPC.
On-tag user memory holds tamper-evident expiration-date offset or partial encrypted serial allowing receiving warehouse to validate before backend round-trip.
M750's 32 bits sufficient for 4-byte timestamp offset + small validation token.
Higher-memory user-data programmes specify Higgs-9 (688-bit user) or UCODE 9 (32-224 bit configurable).

brief.label: Returnable transit items (RTI) cycle authentication
items: RTI tagging benefits from periodic AUTHENTICATE verification to detect counterfeit RTI insertion.
M750 AUTHENTICATE runs in <50 ms per tag; integrates cleanly into pallet-portal inventory cycles.
Each cycle, returning RTI scans authenticate the chip; failed authentications flag potential counterfeits or tampering.

brief.label: Where M750 is NOT the right fit
items: Pure SGTIN-96 retail volume tagging: M750 silicon ASP roughly 30-40% higher than M730. If application doesn't actually use AUTHENTICATE, Untraceable, or user memory, M730 is the correct cost-optimised choice.

Maximum sensitivity / longest read range: M750 trades ~0.6 dB sensitivity for cryptographic feature circuitry. Where every dB matters (small-antenna, on-metal extreme), Alien Higgs-9 (-24.0 dBm) or UCODE 9 (-23.0 dBm) better fit.
Sensor / moisture-detection: no sensor variant in M750 line. UCODE 9xe is the choice.

Bank-grade per-message signing (luxury anti-counterfeit): M750 AUTHENTICATE is chip-authenticity primitive, not per-message signature. For per-message AES-128 signing with read-counter binding (UHF analogue of NTAG424 DNA SUN), step up to NXP UCODE DNA.

brief.label: Procurement and lead times
items: MOQ 10,000 pieces for stock antenna designs.
Lead time 4-6 weeks for stock antenna (slightly longer than M730's 3-4 weeks due to AUTHENTICATE-key provisioning at the chip level).
Custom antenna designs: MOQ 50,000-100,000 pieces; tooling 6-10 weeks + production 2-4 weeks.
Impinj Authenticity service integration: registration step coordinated as part of first production batch.

heroPoints: Cryptographic AUTHENTICATE (AES-128 per GS1 Crypto Suite 3) — chip-level challenge-response proves silicon is genuine Impinj R6-P, not relabelled lower-grade chip. Foundation for UHF brand-protection programmes; pairs with Impinj's Authenticity cloud service for turnkey verification without an HSM.

EPC Gen2v2 Untraceable command — at POS or on-exit, chip can be commanded to return shortened EPC, hide TID, hide user memory until next power cycle. Standard implementation pattern for retail privacy under GDPR-aware EU deployments. Crypto Suite 3 + AES-128 + 32-bit user memory + 96-bit EPC.

EU Digital Product Passport (Regulation 2024/1781) UHF tier — 32-bit user memory holds DPP URL pointer / hash + AUTHENTICATE proves carrier authenticity (anti-substitution). Minimum-feature DPP-compliant UHF chip; step up to UCODE 9 (224-bit configurable user) for full DPP URL + serial + sustainability fields on-tag.

sections.title: What the AES-128 AUTHENTICATE challenge actually proves

dataHighlight.heading: Chip-authenticity verification round-trip via Impinj Authenticity cloud
dataHighlight.text: AUTHENTICATE is a chip-authenticity primitive — not a per-message signature. The reader issues a challenge nonce; the M750 silicon responds with an AES-128 CMAC computed against a pre-loaded chip-specific key. The reader posts the (nonce, response) pair to the Impinj Authenticity cloud REST API, which validates the CMAC against the chip's registered key and returns 'authentic' / 'not authentic' / 'unknown' in under 200 ms typical. The mechanism rejects relabelled M730 silicon (the most common counterfeit pattern) because the chip cannot produce a valid CMAC response without the registered key — and the key is provisioned at Impinj's wafer fab, not field-injectable. The trust chain is: the brand owner trusts Impinj's wafer fab + the Authenticity cloud service. For applications where that's insufficient (luxury / banking / passport-grade), specify NXP UCODE DNA which provides per-message AES-128 signing with read-counter binding (the UHF analogue of NTAG424 DNA SUN messages). M750 + Authenticity is the right answer for mainstream brand-protection where 'cryptographic but not bank-grade' is sufficient.

faq.question: Is Impinj M750 the same as Monza R6-P?
faq.answer: Yes — Impinj rebranded Monza R6-P silicon as M750 under the M700-series naming refresh. Datasheets, EPC Gen2v2 feature support, and TID prefix unchanged. Existing readers, encoders, and inlays branded as Monza R6-P interoperate with M750 inlays.

faq.question: How does M750 differ from NXP UCODE 9?
faq.answer: Both implement EPC Gen2v2 Untraceable + AUTHENTICATE + Crypto Suite 3. Differences: UCODE 9 has more configurable user memory (32-224 bits vs M750's fixed 32 bits), supports Hide-EPC (M750 doesn't), and offers Self-Adjust auto-detune (vs Impinj AutoTune). M750 has the Impinj Authenticity cloud service available out-of-the-box; UCODE 9 deployments either operate their own KMS or use a third-party. Choose by inlay supplier preference and whether you need >32 bits of user memory.

faq.question: Can I use M750 with my existing Impinj reader fleet for AUTHENTICATE?
faq.answer: Yes — EPC Gen2v2 AUTHENTICATE is supported by Impinj R700-series and R420-series fixed readers and the IPJ-R0510 handheld with current firmware (Octane / xArray Octane). If reader fleet predates 2018, firmware update may be needed to access AUTHENTICATE; basic read/write of M750 EPC works on any standards-compliant reader without changes.

faq.question: What is the silicon ASP premium of M750 vs M730?
faq.answer: Indicative pricing at 1M pieces: M730 ~USD 0.018, M750 ~USD 0.024 — roughly a 30% premium for AUTHENTICATE + Untraceable + 32-bit user memory. At 10M+ pieces the premium narrows. For applications that genuinely need any of the three added features, the premium is well worth it; for pure SGTIN-96 retail volume, M730 is the right choice.

faq.question: Does M750 support the EU Digital Product Passport (DPP)?
faq.answer: Yes — M750 meets the minimum-feature UHF DPP profile: 32-bit user memory holds the DPP URL pointer or hash, AUTHENTICATE proves the chip is genuine (anti-substitution), and EPC Gen2v2 compliance ensures global reader interoperability. For DPP profiles requiring larger on-tag data (full DPP URL + serial + sustainability fields), step up to NXP UCODE 9 with 224-bit configurable user memory. EU Regulation 2024/1781 (ESPR) is the underlying mandate framework.

faq.question: What MOQ does Proud Tek offer for M750 inlays?
faq.answer: 10,000 pieces for stock antenna designs. The slightly longer 4-6 week lead time (vs M730's 3-4 weeks) reflects AUTHENTICATE-key provisioning at the chip level. For Impinj Authenticity service integration, Proud Tek coordinates the registration step on the brand owner's behalf as part of the first production batch.
